context_description: A lobby seating cluster placed at the building entrance, giving arriving visitors a place to pause and wait before continuing into the building.

expected_patterns.name: Arrival Transition Seating
expected_patterns.rationale: Classic pattern found in hospitality and corporate architecture; focuses on the specific role of seating as a transitional element at entry points.

expected_patterns.name: Perch and Wait Node
expected_patterns.rationale: Draws on Christopher Alexander's 'A Place to Wait' pattern and workplace research on lobby behavior; specific to seating arrangement within lobbies.

expected_patterns.name: Social Magnet Anchor
expected_patterns.rationale: Common in contemporary workplace and hospitality design; the pattern describes seating not as mere functional furniture but as a generator of social life.

notes: Space-type case. All three expected patterns are attached to this entity in the extracted corpus and should be returned by `bsos query --type pattern --include-proposed`.

context_description: A narrow-lot row house, deep from front to back, at risk of single-aspect rooms and a dead-end plan with no view through to the garden.

expected_patterns.name: Daylight Core Ventilation
expected_patterns.rationale: Classic problem in narrow-lot row houses and townhouses solved through atria and light courts. Widely documented in pattern language literature and vernacular architecture.

expected_patterns.name: Front-to-Back Flow and View
expected_patterns.rationale: Draws on the enfilade tradition in narrow townhouses and modern strategies for connecting interior to garden. Common in Dutch row houses and contemporary narrow-house designs.

notes: Space-type case (a dwelling configuration). Both expected patterns are attached to this entity in the extracted corpus.

context_description: A single fixed bench bolted flush against a blank corridor wall, facing the opposite wall, with no offset, no armrests, and no other seats nearby.

expected_patterns.name: Social Spine Bench
expected_patterns.rationale: Drawn from ethnographic studies of seating behaviour in public buildings (Whyte, Sommer) — perpendicular orientation is a known solution for balancing sociopetal and sociofugal forces. Directly addresses the specific fixed-bench condition where users cannot reposition.

expected_patterns.name: Edge Condition Buffer
expected_patterns.rationale: Rooted in Alexander's 'Building Edge' pattern and confirmed by post-occupancy studies of public plazas. The specific 300-600mm offset with planting is a well-documented fix for the 'bench against wall' failure mode observed in countless institutional buildings.

expected_patterns.name: Windows Overlooking Life
expected_patterns.rationale: A bench facing a blank wall has nothing worth watching; seating should be placed where it overlooks activity. Domain judgement; may be absent from the extracted corpus and reported as missing.

notes: Component-type case. 'Social Spine Bench' and 'Edge Condition Buffer' are attached to this entity in the corpus; 'Windows Overlooking Life' is a reviewer expectation that may be reported missing — that gap is the regression signal.

context_description: A single all-air HVAC system serving every orientation identically with no zoning, and no strategy for shedding heat overnight before the next day's cooling load.

expected_patterns.name: Thermal Zoning by Orientation and Use
expected_patterns.rationale: Standard architectural HVAC design principle codified in ASHRAE Standard 90.1 and taught in mechanical engineering curricula; supported by extensive simulation and case study evidence.

expected_patterns.name: Night Ventilation Cooling (Structural Thermal Flywheel)
expected_patterns.rationale: Well-researched passive cooling strategy documented extensively in building science literature (e.g., work by Givoni, Santamouris) with proven performance in monitoring studies of European and American office buildings.

expected_patterns.name: Economizer Free-Cooling Mode
expected_patterns.rationale: An air-side economizer would let the single all-air system draw on cool outside air directly instead of running compressors year-round. Domain judgement; not present in the extracted corpus and expected to be reported missing.

notes: System-type case. 'Thermal Zoning by Orientation and Use' and 'Night Ventilation Cooling' are attached to this entity in the corpus; 'Economizer Free-Cooling Mode' is a reviewer expectation that may be reported missing — that gap is the regression signal.
